1.say: 'The grant was a shot in the arm for the whole programme.' It is a dead metaphor. Nobody sees an arm. Nobody sees anything, which is why it is safe and dull. Now read me the next line. 'It gave the programme a shot in the arm and a firm foundation to build on.' And there the dead one wakes up. An arm with a foundation under it. I did not see that. You will now. A mixed metaphor is what happens when two dead ones are laid end to end. What about a live one? 'The report is a room with one door.' You can see it, and it can be wrong. A live metaphor is a claim. Sarah opened her review with 'the ending is not earned'. Which brings a whole world in with it in three words: payment, work, deserving. That is allusion doing the same job in less space.

grammar.label: metaphor that is alive, dead or mixed
grammar.form: a live metaphor; a dead one absorbed into the language; two live ones colliding
grammar.meaning: carries meaning by comparison, or fails visibly by mixing pictures

explanation.en: 'Grasp an idea' is a dead metaphor and nobody sees a hand. 'A shot in the arm for the industry' is half alive, which is why 'a shot in the arm that will bear fruit' collapses. The test is simple and nobody applies it: draw the picture. If two pictures appear, rewrite.
explanation.uz: 'Grasp an idea' — o'lik metafora, hech kim qo'lni ko'rmaydi. Sinov oddiy: rasmini chizing. Ikki rasm chiqsa, qayta yozing.

grammar.positive_example: The policy was a shot in the arm for the industry.
grammar.negative_example: The policy was a shot in the arm that would bear fruit down the line.

l1_notes.uz: Metafora aralashuvi ingliz tilida kulgili xato hisoblanadi; tarjimada u ko'pincha sezilmay qoladi.

grammar.label: allusion — borrowing a whole context in three words
grammar.form: a phrase that carries its source with it
grammar.meaning: brings a second text into the sentence without quoting it

explanation.en: An allusion works only for a reader who knows the source, and fails silently for everyone else — they read a slightly odd phrase and move on. That makes it the most exclusive device in the language: it flatters those who catch it and quietly excludes those who do not. Use it knowing exactly who is being left out.
explanation.uz: Allyuziya faqat manbani biladigan o'quvchi uchun ishlaydi va boshqalar uchun jimgina muvaffaqiyatsiz bo'ladi. Shuning uchun u tildagi eng 'yopiq' vosita.

grammar.positive_example: The minister's finest hour lasted about a fortnight.
grammar.negative_example: The minister's finest hour, as Churchill said in 1940, lasted a fortnight.

l1_notes.uz: Allyuziya madaniy bilimga bog'liq; boshqa madaniyatdan kelgan o'quvchi uchun u butunlay ko'rinmas bo'ladi.

body.text: 'The grant was a shot in the arm for the whole programme.'

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: It is a dead metaphor. Nobody sees an arm.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Nobody sees anything, which is why it is safe and dull. Now read me the next line.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: 'It gave the programme a shot in the arm and a firm foundation to build on.'

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: And there the dead one wakes up. An arm with a foundation under it.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: You will now. A mixed metaphor is what happens when two dead ones are laid end to end.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: 'The report is a room with one door.' You can see it, and it can be wrong. A live metaphor is a claim.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Sarah opened her review with 'the ending is not earned'.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Which brings a whole world in with it in three words: payment, work, deserving. That is allusion doing the same job in less space.
